children.text: Every route, section, link and media dimension is settled in the content model. The frontend consumes a resolved shape and never guesses.

items.question: What is a closed section set?

children.text: A curated list of section types the page builder accepts. Adding one is a deliberate decision, not a side effect.
No. Each section validates its own constraints before publish, and every page type scopes which sections it allows.

items.question: Does the frontend need defensive checks?

children.text: It reads a stable, fully resolved shape from GROQ fragments. Dimensions, links and SEO are decided in the CMS.

heading.text: A small studio with strong opinions about content.

children.text: We build sites where the CMS is treated as a product: explicit document roles, factories for every primitive, and a composition layer editors trust.
How we work
Surface before schema. Editors experience navigation, entry points and labels, so we design the Studio first and let the schema follow.
Every primitive is a factory. A link, a piece of media, a heading: defined once, configured per call, never copied.
The frontend consumes, it never assumes. By the time data reaches a component, there is nothing left to decide.

children.text: From a blank Sanity project to a launched site with an agent-ready surface.
One week of interviews with editors and developers to write the document roles as contracts before any schema exists.
Factories, sections and validation rules, reviewed with editors in Presentation as they land.
A thin route layer on top of resolved GROQ shapes, with Markdown negotiation and llms.txt for agents.
Docs, plop generators and scoped agent skills so the next change extends the system instead of renegotiating it.
We take on a small number of engagements per quarter.

title: Designing content models that do not rot
excerpt: Pages, articles and global configuration as explicit contracts instead of loose collections of fields.
author: Ada Northwind

children.text: A page has three responsibilities: identity, composition and discoverability. They evolve independently, so they live in separate tabs.
Articles as a publishing contract
An article reuses the same page builder, scoped to editorial sections, and adds authorship, categories and a publication date. Neither bleeds into the other.
Global configuration as a boundary
If a decision affects the entire site it lives in the Site document. Pages consume navigation; they do not own it.
The remaining parts cover page composition and content primitives.

title: Why the section set is closed
excerpt: A page builder with a curated catalogue, validated constraints and per-type scoping is smaller than an open one, and that is exactly what makes it usable.
author: Ada Northwind

children.text: Sections are easy to add and almost impossible to retire. The moment one ships on a page in production, removing it becomes a migration.
Limits are part of the model
A hero requires a heading, a call to action accepts one or two buttons, a logo grid wants between three and twelve logos. The CMS validates these before publish so the frontend never has to.
Scoping per page type
Articles whitelist editorial sections. Legal pages blacklist anything promotional. The choice is removed at the point of authoring.

items.question: We need a custom HTML block for edge cases.

children.text: Once an escape hatch exists, the discipline of the composition layer is optional. Model a proper section or push back.
Editors stop guessing which sections are safe. The schema answers it for them.
